title: VPN keepalive fallback runbook — early draft
content:
Purpose:
This is an early draft for a runbook that SREs can use when the Private/VPC control plane experiences transient reachability loss caused by VPN or customer-managed firewall behavior that drops or reorders keepalive/heartbeat traffic. The runbook outlines diagnostics, fast mitigations, automated fallback suggestions (gateway-level keepalive vs. application-level heartbeats), and test steps to validate mitigations.

Scope / when to use:
- Control plane API or streaming RPCs intermittently fail for a subset of tenants while data plane stays OK.
- Symptoms: rapid reconnects, apparently healthy tunnels from infra metrics but sudden control RPC timeouts, increase in TCP RSTs between controlplane <-> tenant-proxy, or long SYN->SYN/ACK gaps.
- Not for full fabric outages (use normal incident playbooks). This is for keepalive/heartbeat-specific reachability degradation.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Confirm incident: check controlplane request error rates and the per-tenant route map in Console -> Private -> Connections. Screenshot or copy-relevant graphs.
2) Identify affected tenant(s) and timestamp of first failing request.
3) Check controlplane -> proxy TCP metrics: retransmit rate, RTO, SYN retransmits (observability/metrics).
4) Check the tenant-facing tunnel state (WireGuard/IPsec/BGP) reported by private-agent: last handshake time, conntrack expiry, and kernel counters.
5) Run fast packet-level probe from controlplane host to tenant-proxy private IP: traceroute -T -p <port> and hping3 -S --fast --count 50 -p <port> <tenant-ip>. Note any observed RSTs or absence of SYN/ACK.

Hypotheses to consider (ordered by frequency seen in oncall):
- Customer firewall is running an aggressive SYN proxy or application-layer proxy that fails to forward TCP keepalive (SYN) or silently drops small keepalive packets.
- Intermediate NAT device / service provider performing flow timeouts shorter than controlplane keepalive interval (e.g., 60s) causing mid-session state loss and asymmetric routing on re-establishment.
- MTU / fragmentation issues causing small controlplane heartbeats to be dropped when DF is set.
- Middlebox deep-packet inspection (DPI) is reassembling/reordering keepalive packets causing garbage on arrival to control proxy.
- Kernel-level conntrack exhaustion on tenant or controlplane hosts causing random flows to be dropped.

Fast mitigations (prioritized):
A) Immediately switch the affected tenant(s) to fallback keepalive mode (if enabled): increase keepalive frequency at the per-tenant proxy to 15s for the next 10m. Command (controlplane-admin): 
  curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/tenants/<id>/settings -d '{"keepalive_interval":15, "keepalive_mode":"freq-fallback"}'
Notes: this reduces connection idle timeout on middleboxes but increases controlplane token churn/cost. Only for emergency.

B) If BGP session is used and flaps on control channel, temporarily enable soft-restart/fast-reconnect on the controlplane side while debugging tenant firewall logs.

C) Suggest tenant ops to add a short-lived inbound ACL allowing controlplane ephemeral ports or to disable SYN proxy for a short window. Provide template ACL (example for common firewall vendors below).

D) If conntrack metrics are high, rotate the private-agent process on the tenant host (graceful restart) to clear stuck entries. Command: systemctl restart private-agent.service (coordinate with customer).

Diagnostic commands & observability queries:
- From controlplane host: ss -tanp state established sport = :<port> or ss -o state established to see timers.
- tcpdump: sudo tcpdump -i <if> host <tenant-ip> and port <port> -w /tmp/cp-tenant.pcap (collect ~30s) then scp to analysis node and open with tshark.
- hping3 test: hping3 -S -p <port> -c 30 --fast <tenant-ip> (watch for SYN/ACKs).
- conntrack: sudo conntrack -L | grep <tenant-ip> and sudo conntrack -S for counters.
- eBPF path tracing (if enabled): /opt/tools/trace-tcp-path.sh <tenant-ip> <port> (captures kernel-level drops).
- Observability queries: error rate by tenant, avg latency p50/p95, controlplane connect failures per region (Grafana dashboards).

Customer communication template (short):
Subject: Brief controlplane disruption investigation — action requested
Hi <Customer-SRE>,
We observed intermittent controlplane connectivity issues for tenant <tenant-id> starting at <time>. Symptoms are consistent with an aggressive TCP/SYN proxy or flow timeout on an intermediate firewall/NAT. Could you temporarily: 1) allow TCP flows from controlplane public IPs (list attached) to <tenant-proxy-ip>:<port> for 20 minutes, or 2) disable SYN proxy on that policy for the same window?
We can enable a short-lived keepalive fallback on our side to reduce re-establish intervals while you test.
Thanks — Maya (SRE)
notes_to_self:
- Validate that keepalive fallback is exposed in the admin API with RBAC before enabling in prod.
- Run a canary on Dedicated region us-west-2 for 24h after enabling fallback for a customer with permissive NAT to measure false positives.
- Coordinate with Product about long-term: add per-tenant configurable keepalive profiles (15s/30s/60s) behind feature flag.
- Add unit test to controlplane-proxy to simulate SYN-proxy RST behavior and ensure reconnect backoff behaves correctly.
open_questions: Do we have a full list of public IPs used by controlplane in every region? (needed for customer ACL template)
What telemetry will show SYN-proxy drops vs. NAT timeout? (packet captures + TCP timestamps?)
Who owns the RBAC for controlplane-admin API to allow oncall to toggle fallback?
post_action_items: Add runbook test playbook and a scheduled quarterly fire drill (owner: SRE-runbooks)
Create a small automator to run tcpdump->tshark on first sign of keepalive failures and upload to our incident bucket
Follow up with product on per-tenant keepalive feature and risk assessment
